title: Sinner Was One Game From Victory. Then He Lost Eighteen Straight Points. The World Number One Is Out of the French Open.
excerpt: Juan Manuel Cerundolo completed the most improbable comeback in Grand Slam history as Sinner collapsed in ninety-degree Paris heat. Both top seeds are gone. Djokovic at thirty-nine is the last major champion standing.
body:
The scoreline will take years to fully absorb. Jannik Sinner, the world number one, the four-time Grand Slam champion, the man who had not lost a match in four months, walked onto Court Philippe-Chatrier leading 6-3, 6-2, 5-1 against Juan Manuel Cerundolo. He was one game from the third round. He was the heaviest favourite on the planet, priced at -10000 by sportsbooks — a $5,000 bet to win $50.

Then he lost eighteen straight points.

Then he lost the match.

The Collapse

Cerundolo, ranked 56th in the world, had won three games in two sets. The Argentine was being dismantled. But serving for the match at 5-1 in the third set, Sinner's body began to betray him. His legs stiffened. His movement shortened. His serve, which had been a weapon all afternoon, lost its bite.

What followed was one of the most extraordinary unravellings in Grand Slam history. Cerundolo broke back. Then broke again. Then again. Sinner called for a medical timeout between sets, disappearing off court for treatment while the crowd at Roland Garros sat in stunned silence. The temperature on court had exceeded thirty-three degrees Celsius. The clay radiated heat like a furnace.

It did not matter. Sinner returned and lost the fourth set 1-6. He lost the fifth set 1-6. The final scoreline — 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1 — reads like a misprint.

"I was a little bit lucky and I feel sorry for him," Cerundolo said afterward. "He was serving to win the match. Then I don't know what happened. I think he was cramping. Of course I feel sorry for him and I hope he recovers."

A Record That May Never Be Matched

It is the first time in the Open Era that a men's number one seed has lost the French Open after leading by two sets. It is believed to be the first time any player has lost eighteen consecutive points from such a commanding position at a Grand Slam. Sinner's thirty-match winning streak, which stretched back to February, is over.

ESPN tennis analyst Jim Courier called the medical timeout "absolute baloney," questioning whether Sinner should have been allowed to leave the court for treatment. The rules controversy will echo through the locker room for days.

For Sinner, it is the cruelest possible end to a quest that had defined his 2026 season. He had already won the Australian Open and the Indian Wells Masters. Roland Garros was the only major he had never won. A victory in Paris would have made him the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam since Rod Laver.

Both Top Seeds Gone

The French Open draw is now in unprecedented territory. Carlos Alcaraz, the defending champion and second seed, was already eliminated in the first round. With Sinner gone, neither of the top two seeds will be in the third round. It has not happened at Roland Garros since the seedings era began.

Novak Djokovic, thirty-nine years old and playing in his record-equalling twenty-second main draw at Roland Garros, is suddenly the last remaining major champion in the men's bracket. On Thursday he beat French hope Valentin Royer to reach the third round, saving match points and grinding through a four-set match that ended only as the shadows lengthened across Court Suzanne-Lenglen.

Djokovic is now the oldest realistic contender to win the tournament since Jimmy Connors reached the semifinals of the US Open at thirty-nine in 1991. If he lifts the trophy on June 7, it would be his twenty-fifth Grand Slam title and arguably the most improbable of them all.

What NRIs Should Know

For the millions of Indian tennis fans who have followed this sport through the Paes-Bhupathi era and into the age of Djokovic, Sinner, and Alcaraz, this is the most wide-open Grand Slam in memory. The French Open is being broadcast on Eurosport and discovery+ in India, with most matches available in the early evening IST window.

Indian doubles pair Yuki Bhambri and Sriram Balaji are still alive in the men's doubles draw, having won their second-round match on Day 3.

The draw that was supposed to produce a Sinner-Djokovic semifinal now has a gaping hole at the top. Third seed Alexander Zverev, who has never won a major, is the highest seed remaining on Sinner's side. The quarter that Sinner vacated is now occupied by Cerundolo, the accidental giant-killer from Buenos Aires.

The 2026 French Open was already the wildest Grand Slam in a generation before Thursday. Seventeen players withdrew before the tournament began. Four collapsed in the heat during the first week. Now the biggest casualty of all has fallen.

Paris, as it turns out, takes no prisoners. Not even the best player on the planet.
